children.text: A canyoning effect happens if the license plate is placed close to the sensor with canyon aperture in line with sensor or license plate (holder) and parts that act as a 'resonant box' (see Figure 10 ). Therefore, special considerations shall be given if the sensors are placed next to the mentioned parts. The action to avoid the canyoning effect must be agreed with Continental in an early stage of development. Possible actions are to place the sensors outside the main reflection directions that are marked with red color in Figure 10 or to move the sensor in front to have the canyoning structure behind the sensor surface.

9.2 Vehicle FoV Test (ISO 17386)

The vehicle field of view test is conducted after the simulation when a first bumper design is available. The output of the coverage simulator and the placement of the sensors at the vehicle bumper can be verified by measuring the static detection field of view of the ultrasonic sensor system. In this test norm objects are placed in a 10 cm raster in the whole field of view of the vehicle bumper. For each new object position the detection of the sensors are evaluated. In this way restrictions and gaps in the field of view due to the application of the sensors can be detected.

The output of the coverage simulator and the placement of the sensors at the vehicle bumper can be verified by measuring the static detection field of view of the ultrasonic sensor system. In this test norm objects are placed in a 10 cm raster in the whole field of view of the vehicle bumper. For each new object position the detection of the sensors are evaluated. In this way restrictions and gaps in the field of view due to the application of the sensors can be detected.
